content: Physical Indivisibility and Sale of the Inheritance Asset Following the death of a testator, several heirs (husband, daughters, and grandchildren) sought the dissolution of the inheritance community regarding the sole estate asset, an apartment in Rome. The legal classification involves the "scioglimento della comunione ereditaria" and the assessment of "comoda divisibilità". The interpretative challenge lies in determining whether the property's internal layout and consistency allow for a physical division into autonomous shares without compromising its utility. Based on the Court-appointed expert's findings, the apartment was deemed not conveniently divisible in kind. Furthermore, since no co-heir insisted on the full attribution of the asset (assignment) with the payment of cash equalizations, the Court applied the principle that an indivisible property must be sold via judicial auction to distribute the proceeds among the co-heirs according to their respective quotas.
